question: Yesterday you ran a named session, energy-policy-review, in which the document analysis agent examined 40 source files for a research report. Overnight, a colleague replaced three of those files with revised versions, and the other 37 files did not change. You resume the session with --resume energy-policy-review to continue the work. What is the most effective way to proceed?

options.text: Tell the resumed session which three files were revised and ask it to re-analyze only those files before continuing.
options.reason: The guide says to inform a resumed session about specific file changes so that it re-analyzes them in a targeted way instead of re-exploring everything.

options.text: Continue the resumed session without mentioning the revisions, because the agent will detect changed files when it next reads them.
options.reason: The guide stresses informing the agent about changes to previously analyzed files. Without that information, the agent may rely on stale results for the three revised files.

options.text: Discard the named session and start a new one that explores all 40 files from scratch without any prior context.
options.reason: Most of the prior context is still valid, so the guide favors resuming the session. This option throws away valid work and repeats a full exploration.

options.text: Ask the resumed session to re-read and re-analyze all 40 files so that every finding reflects the current versions of the documents.
options.reason: This forces a full re-exploration, although the analysis of the 37 unchanged files is still valid. The guide prefers a targeted re-analysis of only the changed files.
